abstract: The existing card based parking system at shopping malls requires staff to hand out parking cards, makes customers search for free slots by themselves, and only reveals parking fees at the exit gantry. This project proposes M-parking, a mobile application for Android phones with NFC that lets members check in and check out by tapping their phone at the gantry. The system recommends a parking zone based on the store the customer wants to visit or the first available zone from the lowest floor upward, and members can view their parking time and fees during the session. A web application lets the administrator manage customers, staff, zones, slots, stores, floor plans, and parking rates, and produce daily and monthly parking reports. The proposed system is analyzed and designed using data flow diagrams, an entity relationship diagram, and a data dictionary.

abstract: Marathon running has grown quickly in Thailand, but existing websites only list events with brief information and links, show routes as static map images, and keep no record of runners once an event ends. This project built a web based management system where runners can register, view event information and routes, join events, see ranks, and find photos tagged to them. Administrators can create and manage events, build event routes with Google My Maps, enter finish times that automatically generate ranks, and tag runners in event photos. The website was developed with WordPress and the EventOn event calendar plugin, customized with PHP and database modifications. Test cases for user registration, login, event registration, and runner management all passed.

abstract: Apartment managers in Thailand still keep tenant information, contracts, and utility records on paper, which can be lost or damaged and leads to calculation mistakes. This project develops a web based apartment management system that runs on the apartment local area network for the manager and staff. The system records rooms, tenants, and contracts, calculates electricity and water bills, tracks payments and expenses, checks room availability, and prints ready to sign contracts and invoices. It also generates monthly utility and summary reports for the manager. The system is written in PHP with a MySQL database, uses Bootstrap for the interface template, runs on AppServ with the Apache web server, and generates PDF files with FPDF.

abstract: Buyers face many smartphone models with different features and it is difficult to pick one that fits their preferences and budget. Phonies is a proposed website where users can browse smartphone specifications, compare models side by side, and get a product recommendation. The matching system pairs smartphones with the lifestyle favorites stored in a member profile or entered directly, filtered by the desired budget, and also ranks products by popularity based on member clicks. Administrators can add, update, and delete products with correct specifications and reliable images. The system is planned as an online web application written in PHP with a MySQL database administered through phpMyAdmin and hosted on Z.com hosting.

abstract: Thailand has many websites with game news and ratings but none that gathers game promotions in one place, so gamers miss limited time deals and must search each game company site themselves. This project built a game promotion website where visitors and members can browse games, view promotion details, and read game news. Members can rate games on graphics, audio, and gameplay, write comments, and subscribe to games to receive notification of new promotions. Administrators manage games, promotions, and member accounts through the backend. The website is developed in PHP with a MySQL database.
